# Sprout Social Cuts 260 Jobs in Major Workforce Reduction Amid AI Transformation  
Sprout Social announced on July 15, 2026, that it is laying off 260 employees, representing 20% of its total workforce. The enterprise social media management company joins a growing list of tech firms restructuring operations as artificial intelligence reshapes the industry. The cuts signal a significant strategic pivot for the Chicago-based company, which has faced mounting pressure to reduce costs and accelerate its AI-driven product roadmap. The layoffs reflect broader tech industry trends that have seen companies aggressively trim headcount to fund automation investments and satisfy investor demands for profitability.
## Impact on Operations  
The 260 affected employees span multiple departments, with the heaviest cuts falling in areas where AI automation now handles core functions. Sales support, customer success, and certain marketing operations roles saw significant reductions. Engineering teams focused on legacy infrastructure were also affected as the company consolidates resources around its next-generation AI product suite.  
Sprout Social's primary operations are based in Chicago, Illinois, with additional teams working remotely across North America and in international markets. The layoffs affect employees across these locations. Affected workers received notification on July 15, 2026, and the company indicated it would provide severance packages and career transition support.  
The remaining workforce of approximately 1,040 employees will focus on core platform development, enterprise sales, and AI product expansion.

The practical read for a buyer: if your service is delivered from Europe, treat end of Q3 2026 as the earliest date your account coverage changes, not the date it settles. The same day, the Chicago-based social-media management vendor filed a Form 8-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Employee notifications had started that morning.
The board had approved the plan a week earlier, on 8 July. What makes the day unusual is what else sat in the document. Under Item 2.02, the company said it "expects its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 to be at the high end of its financial outlook ranges for revenue, non-GAAP operating income, and non-GAAP net income per share." results.name: Sprout Social to cut 260 jobs as AI reshapes software industry
results.content:
Sprout Social is laying off about 20% of its workforce, affecting roughly 260 employees, as the social media management company restructures its business amid rapid changes across the software industry.  
The company began notifying affected employees on Wednesday. Chief Executive Ryan Barretto said the decision reflects broader shifts in how software companies are operating as artificial intelligence reshapes business priorities and investment strategies.  
“Our industry, and software more broadly, is changing quickly,” he said. “The way companies need to operate and invest has changed with it.”  
**READ: Meta layoff forces H-1B worker to leave US** (July 14, 2026)  
The [layoffs](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/sprout-social-to-cut-20-of-workforce-as-ai-fueled-tech-layoffs-continue-7e2b1b17?mod=markets) follow Sprout’s recent push into AI. In May, the company introduced an AI-powered social intelligence platform aimed at helping businesses better manage their social media presence. It also expanded Trellis, its agentic AI engine, with new capabilities for publishing content and analyzing social media data.  
Sprout joins a growing list of technology companies that have cited AI-driven changes while reducing headcount. Oracle said in June that it eliminated 21,000 jobs as it redirected spending toward AI initiatives. Cisco and Meta have also announced workforce reductions of 20% and 10%, respectively, while pointing to evolving business priorities.
Among the largest layoffs this year, Block, the parent company of Square and Cash App, said it would cut 40% of its workforce, stating that AI had fundamentally changed how the company operates.  
**READ: Wells Fargo layoffs renew debate over H-1B hiring** (June 22, 2026)  
Sprout expects the restructuring to result in pre-tax charges of between $18 million and $20 million, largely related to severance and employee benefits. The company said most of those costs will be recorded during the third quarter, when the layoffs are expected to be completed.  
Employees affected by the cuts will receive 12 weeks of base pay, plus an additional week of salary for each year of service. The company will also provide six months of fully paid healthcare coverage, a cash payment equal to the value of equity scheduled to vest over the next 90 days, and three months of outplacement assistance.  
The announcement comes after Sprout reported stronger financial performance in its most recent quarter. In May, the company posted higher revenue and a narrower loss. On Wednesday, it also said it expects its results for the quarter ended in June to come in at the high end of its previously issued guidance.

### Notable Software and AI-Related Cuts in Late July 2026  
**ServiceNow** In late July, ServiceNow reduced hundreds of positions as part of a broader effort to streamline operations while accelerating AI investment. Employees described the day of the announcement as particularly difficult. The enterprise workflow software company joins a growing list of SaaS firms adjusting headcount amid pressure to deliver AI-driven efficiency.  
[monday.com](http://monday.com/) The work-management platform announced plans to cut about 20% of its workforce (roughly 620 employees) in a restructuring tied to its “AI-driven growth strategy.” The company said the moves support a leaner, more focused operating model and continued investment in AI capabilities. It expects $45–55 million in restructuring charges while still projecting strong revenue growth.  
**Sprout Social** The social media management software company cut approximately 260 jobs (about 19–20% of its workforce) in mid-July, citing AI-driven changes in the software industry and the need to adapt its cost structure.  
**Other notable activity**  
- Amazon confirmed additional reductions within parts of its AGI (artificial general intelligence) organization in late July, describing the moves as a sharpening of focus even as it continues heavy AI investment.
- Earlier in July, Microsoft eliminated about 4,800 roles (roughly 2.1% of its global workforce), with significant impact on its Xbox gaming division and some commercial functions. Leadership noted that AI is changing how work gets done, though it stated the specific cuts were part of a broader business reset.
- Visa, Thomson Reuters, TikTok, and several other firms announced reductions in July that were linked in part to AI or operational streamlining.  
Smaller software, SaaS, and tech-enabled companies also appeared in July tracking lists, reflecting a pattern of mid-sized firms adjusting headcount while larger peers pour capital into data centers and AI systems.
### Impact on Software Workers  
Entry-level and mid-level software roles have been particularly exposed as code-generation tools and AI agents handle more routine work. Analysts and labor data point to slower hiring and higher displacement risk for junior developers. At the same time, companies emphasize that many cuts free budget for AI investment rather than representing pure replacement of every eliminated role by a model.  
Workers affected by the latest round of cuts typically receive severance packages, outplacement support, and, in some cases, extended benefits. The concentration of reductions in software and SaaS continues to reshape career paths across Silicon Valley, Seattle, Austin, and other U.S. tech hubs.
